lanes.lane: Visual design of components and screens (VIS)
lanes.currentState: The code follows direction C closely, and C is flat on purpose. tokens.generated.ts:828-830 sets effects {gradients:false, textures:false, glows:false}. components.md §0.1 requires every round-1 screen to be translated with "no gradients, no textures, no glows, no skew", and §1.1 adds "No gradient (round 1's gradient and shine are dropped)". motion.md:37 says "Premium comes from timing, not effects". Only the gold primary has depth: it is skewed -8°, sits on a hard 4dp accentShadow edge and has an animated 3dp press (Button.tsx:139-180). Secondary, ghost, IconButton and RowButton are transparent outlines with a 1dp #2a3140 border (Button.tsx:288-295, IconButton.tsx:83-91, RowButton.tsx:89-99). That border measures 1.44:1 against bg, and a card's surface measures 1.09:1 against bg. Tappable cards use three different press styles (opacity .85, surface or surface2) and none of them move or scale. Only Dir-C-Home, Dir-C-Game, Levels-* and Friends-* were drawn in C (checked by background color across docs/design/screens). GameType, Results, Leaderboard, Profile and Modes exist only as round-1 boards, and the translation rule mechanically stripped them: watermark, difficulty pips, hero avatar with crown, victory title, confetti. The store brand (tile-clash 5⚡9, apps/mobile/assets/brand/icon.png, tile-clash.svg) never appears inside the app: Home shows a plain Teko text wordmark. Fonts are Rubik 400-700 and Teko 500/600 only. No screenshots of the running app exist, so these judgments come from code and boards. Every item below needs Moshe's eyes on the phone before rollout. The dev route /dev/design-system (DesignSystemScreen) is the natural place to show the old and new versions side by side.
lanes.verdictOnMosheFeedback:
AGREE, with one nuance. He is right that the design reads as simple and that the buttons are under-invested. The cause is a deliberate rule set, not sloppy building: C's translation rule (components.md §0.1; tokens effects gradients/glows/textures=false, tokens.generated.ts:828-830; motion.md:37) removed round 1's depth everywhere except the gold CTA.

Measured evidence:
- Secondary, icon and row buttons are transparent, and their only boundary is a #2a3140 hairline at 1.44:1 against bg (Button.tsx:288, IconButton.tsx:83, RowButton.tsx:89). Cards sit at 1.09:1 against the ground. They barely exist visually.
- Only the primary animates its press. Every other control just swaps a background color instantly, and three different press styles are mixed: LeaderboardParts.tsx:237 / ResultsVersus.tsx:585 / PlayerCardScreen.tsx:665 use opacity .85, ModesScreen.tsx:713 / ProfileCard.tsx:240 / HistoryCard.tsx:234 use surface2, and GameTypeScreen.tsx:271 / RecentGames.tsx:179 use surface.
- Round 1 had a full tactile system that was dropped: filled secondary with a hard dark edge and an inner highlight, a gradient gold with an inset highlight, and a shine sweep (DS-Components.dc.html:64-91, GameType.dc.html:147).

Moshe's own original spec (00-original-spec-v1.md:31-89, which wins over everything) explicitly asks for "עומק ויזואלי", "Micro-interactions", "כרטיסי שחקנים" and "אפקטים של ניצחון והפסד". It forbids looking like a "Dashboard עסקי", an "אפליקציית Utility" or an "אפליקציית סודוקו בסיסית". So the flat rule is a design-doc choice (made when Claude translated D30), not a spec requirement, and it can be revised.

Nuance:
- The gold primary is already the most invested element. The real gap is the secondary, icon and row controls, the cards, and the screens that were only ever drawn in round 1 (Results, GameType, Leaderboard).
- Keeping his colors is correct. Round 1 was rejected as "too colorful and unclear" (03-DESIGN.md:121), so the depth should come from light and shade within the same hues (highlights, edges, tonal gradients from existing tokens such as accentHover → accent → accentPressed), not from new colors.

proposals.title: Premium tactile button system (layers, states, sizes) in the current colors
proposals.problem: Only the gold primary has depth: a skewed face, a hard 4dp accentShadow edge and a 3dp animated press (Button.tsx:139-180). Its face is a flat fill with no highlight (components.md §1.1 'No gradient'). Secondary, ghost, danger and IconButton are transparent outlines with a 1dp #2a3140 border at 1.44:1 against bg (Button.tsx:288-295, IconButton.tsx:83-95). Their press is an instant bg swap with no motion (Button.tsx:192, 223, 305). Disabled is opacity .4 for every variant (Button.tsx:248), which turns the gold into a muddy olive #6f5e28 (2.95:1 against bg). Primary and secondary sitting side by side do not line up: the skewed face sticks out about 3.4dp at its corners at 48dp height (ModesScreen.tsx:318-329 friends footer; ResultsScreen.tsx actions). One screen also has an ad-hoc flat gold button outside the system (LeaderboardParts.tsx:171, 252).
proposals.proposal:
One `TactileSurface` primitive that every button uses, with the same layer stack: edge, face, highlight, label.

PRIMARY (gold, keeps the -8° skew):
- Edge: the existing 4dp accentShadow block.
- Face: a vertical gradient accentHover #ffe08a (0%) → accent #ffcf3f (50%) → accentPressed #f5c21f (100%). All three are existing tokens, so no new hue.
- Highlight: inset 0 1.5 0 rgba(255,255,255,.55) on the top lip, and inset 0 -2 0 rgba(0,0,0,.10) at the bottom.
- Hero only: a soft warm drop shadow 0 10 24 rgba(255,207,63,.18) (Moshe decides whether to keep this 'glow'), and one sheen sweep when Home gains focus. The sweep is a 35% white diagonal band over 900 ms, not a loop.
- Label: the Rubik 900 display weight from VIS-5. Optional leading icon in onAccent.

SECONDARY ('slate', not skewed):
- Filled surface2 face, 1dp border, a 3dp hard edge in a new token surfaceEdge #0a0c11, and an inset top highlight rgba(255,255,255,.06).
- Label in Rubik 600, color.text.
- Selected: accent border, accentSubtle fill, accent label.

ICON BUTTON: the same slate layers at 44×44 with a 2dp edge.

DANGER: keeps its outline/subtle fill (§6.6 requires 'ביטול' to stay the more prominent button), plus a 2dp edge in dangerShadow at 50%.

GHOST: unchanged, plus a pressedOverlay pill on press.

STATES:
- Pressed: face translateY to the edge (3dp primary, 2dp slate), edge shrinks to 1dp, scale .98 using the existing spring token motion.spring.press, and the face darkens one step. The haptic stays (cue).
- Disabled: no faded gold. The face becomes surface2 with a 1dp border and a textFaint label, there is no edge, the skew is kept, and an optional lock icon shows when the button is gated.
- Loading: unchanged.

SIZES: hero 96 / lg 60 / md 52 / modal 48, plus a new sm 40 (with a 44 hitSlop). The leaderboard 'play' pill moves to sm.

PAIR RULE: when a primary and a secondary share a row, either skew the secondary too (round 1 did this, DS-Components.dc.html:69-70) or inset the primary by tan8°×h/2 so the outer edges align. Moshe picks on the phone.

IMPLEMENTATION: RN 0.86 boxShadow, which supports inset (checked in node_modules StyleSheetTypes.d.ts:343-349 and 516), and experimental_backgroundImage linear-gradient (line 520). react-native-svg LinearGradient is the fallback and is already on the startup path through Icon. Do not use Skia: startupGraph.test.ts keeps it off the Home path. Build it first in /dev/design-system, old and new side by side.

Optional, game lane: give keypad keys the same 2-3dp slate edge. Keypad.tsx:269 already translates keys 3dp on press but they have no base, so the key slides instead of sinking.

proposals.title: One surface ladder and one press language for every tappable card and row
proposals.problem: Similar elements are built three different ways. RowButton and RecentGames rows are transparent with radius 12 (RowButton.tsx:89-99, RecentGames.tsx row). HistoryCard and ModeCard are surface with radius 14 (HistoryCard.tsx card, ModesScreen.tsx card). LeaderboardRow is surface with an invisible border (LeaderboardParts.tsx row). Results tiles are surface2 with no border (ResultsScreen.tsx tile). Presses differ too: opacity .85 (LeaderboardParts.tsx:237, ResultsVersus.tsx:585, PlayerCardScreen.tsx:665), surface2 (ModesScreen.tsx:713, ProfileCard.tsx:240, HistoryCard.tsx:234) or surface (GameTypeScreen.tsx:271, RecentGames.tsx:179). None of them move. surface vs bg is 1.09:1, so cards melt into the ground. The spring.press token exists but only the keypad uses it (components/board/animation.ts:41, Keypad.tsx:285).
proposals.proposal:
Define a three-step elevation ladder in tokens.json, and one `PressableCard` that shares VIS-1's primitive.
- L0 ground: bg (plus VIS-9).
- L1 card: surface, 1dp border whose top edge is one step lighter (a new borderLit token, about #343c4e), an inset top highlight rgba(255,255,255,.05), and a 2dp hard dark base rgba(0,0,0,.35). The base is the same hard-edge idea as the CTA, not a blur.
- L2 control/raised: surface2 with the slate edge from VIS-1.
- L3 sheet/modal: surface plus a real drop shadow 0 -8 24 rgba(0,0,0,.5). Today tokens set sheet/modal shadow to null.

Radii: controls 12, cards 14, sheets 24, as written in components.md §0.4 but applied consistently.

All tappable rows become L1 cards, including Home's 'עוד סיבוב' and the recent rows, which are transparent today. One press behavior everywhere: scale .98, translateY to the base, face to surface2, using spring.press. Selected and checked: accent border plus accentSubtle fill. Disabled and offline keep their current meaning (dashed, .6), drawn on the same ladder.

Apply to: RowButton, ModeCard, TypeCard, HistoryCard, RecentGames rows, LeaderboardRow, the results PlayerRow, ProfileCard, the PlayerCardScreen tiles and the friends FriendsButton.

Inside the app it never appears. tile-clash is referenced only by a test (src/__tests__/appIcons.test.ts:176). Home's header is a plain Teko text wordmark, half gray and half white (HomeScreen.tsx:143-155, :308). Login/Splash uses four 14dp seat glyphs over the same text (account/parts.tsx:446-470). The color.brand tokens (blue, orange, spark, grid) are defined but unused in the app (tokens.generated.ts:223-230; grep finds no color.brand use). The Modes ranked rows' picture is 9dp seat shapes in a 44 box (ModesScreen.tsx:614-634, SEAT_GLYPH=9 at :660). It is the weakest picture on that screen, next to an avatar and a 28dp robot.
proposals.proposal:
1) Home header: replace the text-only wordmark with a 36-40dp tile-clash mark (react-native-svg, the same paths as tile-clash.svg) at the start, with 'SUDOKU FIGHT' beside it. Do the same on Login/Splash at 96dp in place of the seat-glyph row. The app's first screen then matches the icon the player just tapped.

2) Use the tilted digit tile as the app's motif:
- Ranked rows on Modes show 2, 3 or 4 small overlapping tiles rotated ±12°, in the seat ring colors, each with its seat shape (●▲■◆) in place of a digit. This keeps ownership readable without relying on color.
- Empty states (no recent games, empty history) use a tilted tile with the shape or digit.

All of these are static Svg on the existing token colors.

lanes.lane: Motion, game feel ("juice"), haptics and sound
lanes.currentState: In-game motion is rich and follows docs/design/motion.md closely. On the board and HUD: cell flash, digit pop, wrong-digit shake and shrink, my lock's pulse, the last-3-seconds blink and the presence fade (Cell.tsx:219-229, 362-377, 470-484, 685-707, 801-884); key press and the keypad-shuffle slide (Keypad.tsx:226-285); score chips flying on an arc (FlightLayer.tsx); count-up on the UI thread (anim.ts:42-70, CountUpText.tsx); the lead bar re-split (LeadBar.tsx:18-33); Skia interference effects with static Reduced Motion covers (components/interference/*). Match flow: radar sweep, VS slam, 3-2-1-GO slam plus ring (SearchView.tsx:225-246, FoundView.tsx, CountdownView.tsx). Levels: node pulse, star pops, confetti, chapter slam and gate unlock (LevelNode.tsx:164-182, StarRow.tsx:105-135, LevelResultView.tsx:277, ChapterUnlockedView.tsx, GatePlate.tsx:110-143). Results: a fade-down title, rising sections, rating count-up and the winner avatar's idle (ResultsScreen.tsx:466-483, ResultsVersus.tsx:366-433). Screen transitions: native slide for menus, 240 ms fade for the game flow, 140 ms fade for tabs, and fades only under Reduced Motion (app/_layout.tsx:146-160). Reduced Motion: every animated file handles it. The only file with no reduce reference is components/interference/hitClock.ts, which is a clock, not an animation. Haptics (services/haptics.ts) and sound (services/sfx.ts) are wired through cue() (services/feedback.ts) with an 80 ms gap and 'strongest wins'. Gaps: (1) all 32 sounds are synthesized placeholders, each 0.39 s or shorter (sfx.ts:62-95, assets/sounds/README.md, DECISIONS-PENDING 3.2). (2) Every menu and meta screen has zero Reanimated: Home, Modes, GameType, BotSelect, History, Leaderboard, Achievements, Login, LoginArena. (3) Secondary, row, icon and card presses only change background colour, and the settings switch thumb jumps. (4) Several things motion.md specifies are not built: the Results win slam, win confetti, place-badge pop, podium growth, the `go` board reveal, `list.enter`, `progress.fill`, and the stage-result win cue.
lanes.verdictOnMosheFeedback:
I mostly agree. Some of the problem is real motion gaps, and some is perception. In the game itself, motion is not lacking: dozens of animations are built to spec, all with Reduced Motion variants. The app still feels under-animated, for three reasons I can show in the code:

(a) Outside the game everything is static. HomeScreen, ModesScreen, GameTypeScreen, BotSelectScreen, HistoryScreen/HistoryCard, LeaderboardScreen/Parts, app/achievements.tsx, LoginScreen and LoginArena have 0 Reanimated imports. LoginArena.tsx:17 says it outright: "nothing moves". Presses on secondary, row and icon buttons and on selection cards only change background colour (Button.tsx:216-224, RowButton.tsx:60-62, ModesScreen.tsx:713, GameTypeScreen.tsx:271). The settings switch thumb jumps (SettingControls.tsx:37). The XP bar is a static width (screens/progress/parts.tsx:45-47). So Moshe's "the buttons are not invested enough" is accurate.

(b) The big reward moments are under-built compared with the design doc. Results uses the same fade-down title for a win as for a loss (ResultsScreen.tsx:470-473). Confetti is only used in levels (LevelResultView.tsx:277), never on a ranked win. The podium and the final score are static (ResultsVersus.tsx:296, ResultsScreen.tsx:297). There is no board reveal at GO (no use of boardRevealAt or revealStagger outside tokens).

(c) Sound is half of game feel, and every file is a synthesized beep: win.wav 0.39 s, go.wav 0.39 s, and hit_*.wav 0.34-0.39 s for a 5-second effect. Better CC0 candidates already sit in assets/sounds/candidates (go 1.48 s, win 0.91 s, hit_fireworks 2.24 s) but are not used.

The root cause is in the design doc. motion.md §1.4 ("Only functional loops") and §2 ("no textures", decorative loops dropped) deliberately removed ambient motion after round-1 feedback. The original spec §2 explicitly asks for animations, micro-interactions, screen transitions, visual depth and "progress and reward". That rule belongs to the design doc, not the original spec, so it can be relaxed.

Moshe's floating-digits background is feasible and fits the original spec, under conditions: very faint (about 3-5% opacity), only on non-board screens, paused when the screen is not shown, and static under Reduced Motion. It needs his eyes on the A16 for opacity and frame rate. A cheap way to make things feel alive, whatever avatar art ships: AVATAR_STAGES (avatars/reactions.ts:219-227) turns idle animation on per place with one flag (home, profile, search, vs, countdown are all false today).

proposals.problem: Only the primary CTA has press motion (Button.tsx:143-150). proposals.title: Ambient drifting-digits background on non-board screens (Moshe's idea, constrained)
proposals.problem: Every screen background is flat color.bg. In direction C, motion.md §1.4 ('Only functional loops') and §2 (decorative loops and textures dropped) were deliberate after round-1's 'too colorful' feedback. The result is a still, utility-like look. The original spec asks for 'עומק ויזואלי' and a game that does not look like 'אפליקציית סודוקו בסיסית' (00-original-spec-v1.md:44-63).
proposals.proposal: Add an <AmbientDigits/> layer behind content on Splash, Login, Home, Modes, GameType, Match search and Results. Never on GameScreen, the level stages, Replay's board or any sheet over a board. It draws 10-14 glyphs (1-9, Teko 600, 28-64 dp) in color.text at 3-5% opacity, with one or two in P1 or gold at the same faintness. Each drifts on a slow seeded path (20-40 s per loop), and every few seconds one glyph 'hops' and settles (pop spring). The layout is seeded from a fixed table, not Math.random, so screenshots and tests are stable. Props density and tint per screen, settings in a config file. If Moshe goes ahead with the digit-character avatars, this layer can later show their silhouettes.
proposals.specConflict: Conflicts with docs/design/motion.md §1.4 ('Only functional loops') and §2 (decorative idle loops and textures dropped). These are design-doc rules from direction C, not the original spec; the original asks for visual depth and animation (00-original-spec-v1.md:44-74). motion.md needs an amendment that allows ambient motion off the board. The original's 'אסור שהאפקטים יפגעו בקריאות הלוח' is respected by keeping it off every board screen.
proposals.reducedMotionAndPerf: Reduced Motion: the same glyphs drawn static (the texture stays, nothing moves). Perf: drive all glyphs from one useFrameCallback clock with positions computed in a worklet: about 12 transforms, no React renders. Pause when useScreenFocused() is false or the app is backgrounded. Use Animated.Text with the embedded Teko family rather than Skia text: Android release builds don't load fonts in JS (theme/fonts.ts:21-26), which complicates Skia useFont. Measure UI-thread time on the Galaxy A16 (target under 1 ms per frame).

proposals.title: Board-complete wave and unit-complete sweep
proposals.problem: When the board completes, the game holds 1100 ms (correctFlash 700 + LAST_CELL_HOLD 400; screens/game/model.ts:113-115), but only the last cell flashes. The board's biggest moment is one cell. During play, filling a row, column or box shows nothing on the board, though the data is in every correct effect (game/effects.ts:26 breakdown; row/col/box === 8 means the unit is complete). The avatars already treat it as a big moment (avatars/reactions.ts:262 fillsSomething, then 'bigCorrect' at :304).
proposals.proposal: 1) Board complete: during the existing 1100 ms hold, a ripple travels from the last cell outward by Chebyshev ring (about 35 ms per ring, 8 rings). Each cell brightens to its solver's tint and back, and the wave ends in a 1-frame gold board edge. No extra delay before Results. 2) Unit complete during play: one band in the mover's ring colour at 20-25% opacity, under the digits, sweeps along the completed row, column or box in 450 ms. Several units completed by one move play together. Opponents' completions use their colour.
proposals.specConflict: docs/design/motion.md §1 rule 3 ('On the board, only one cell animates at a time') and rule 1 ('Motion never hides the board'). This is a design-doc rule, not the original spec. The original asks that 'שינוי משמעותי במצב המשחק צריך להיות מורגש' while effects must not hurt board readability (00-original-spec-v1.md:79-86), hence the low opacity, under-digit layer and short duration. Scoring nuance: completing a unit is the lowest-scoring move (X=8, spec §14 formula), so the sweep should read as progress, not reward; keep it subtle.

proposals.title: Progress moments: animated XP bar, level-up pop, unlock and achievement toasts

XP, level and achievements update silently in the background after a ranked game (progress/rankedRefresh.ts:13-17), so Home's numbers just change. When Home or the player card regains focus with newer values: the XP bar fills from old to new over 650 ms (scaleX, `standard`) with count ticks. On a level-up: fill to 100%, the level number pops (`pop`), the bar resets and fills to the new share, and a success toast says 'רמה 3!' plus 'נפתחה הפרעה: דיו' when INTERFERENCE_UNLOCK_LEVELS crosses. proposals.title: Lead-flip moment and a cheaper lead bar
proposals.problem: When the lead changes there is a sound, a light haptic for me and a live announcement (GameScreen.tsx:889-904). Visually, the lead tag's border and text tint snap to the new leader's colour (LeadBar.tsx:63, 82) with no motion. LeadBar animates flexGrow (LeadBar.tsx:18-33), a layout property every frame, while motion.md §6 asks for scaleX ('Bars use scaleX, not width').
proposals.proposal: On a leader change, the lead tag pops (`pop`, 0.8 to 1.15 to 1) and cross-fades its colour over 240 ms. When I take the lead, my card's score gets the stronger 1.12 bump. On a tie, the tag does a small 'shrug' (scaleX 1 to 0.9 to 1). Rewrite the segments as scaleX on fixed-width segments with a translateX tag, keeping the visible result.
proposals.reducedMotionAndPerf: Reduced Motion: colour cross-fade only, with no scale (motion.md `leader.change` reduced: cross-fade). Perf: moving from flexGrow to scaleX/translateX removes per-frame layout passes on a screen that already re-renders 4 times a second.

topThree: MOT-1: Real sounds. Every sound is a synthesized beep of 0.39 s or less (win, GO, and the 5-second interference beds included), while better CC0 candidates already sit in the repo. This is the biggest gain in game feel for the effort.

MOT-4: A tactile press system. Only the primary CTA moves when pressed; secondary, row and icon buttons, selection cards and the switch just snap, and 17 of 28 screens with a primary button have no press haptic. This is exactly Moshe's 'the buttons are not invested enough'.
MOT-2: Build the specified Results win timeline (title slam, confetti, badge pop, podium growth, score count-up). Today a ranked win opens with the same fade-down as a loss and no confetti.

lanes.lane: UX flows, first-run experience, navigation and simplicity
lanes.currentState:
The flows are complete and sturdy. There are skeleton, empty, offline and error states almost everywhere (HistoryScreen.tsx:15-23, LeaderboardScreen.tsx:45, ProgressScreen.tsx:104-120, FlowFallback), and the back stack is disciplined (goToTab/goBack in screens/home/navigation.ts). The weak points are teaching, shortcuts and consistency.

Tap counts, from code:

- **Brand-new user, email path.** Splash → Login (auth/redirect.ts:84-89 sends every signed-out player there; there is no guest play, D24 is open but built as "signup required") → "הרשמה" link → Fighter (name, country defaulted) → Account (email, password, confirm password, terms) → Home → "שחק" → Modes (6 rows + 2 friends buttons) → GameType → start. That is about 11 taps and 4 typed fields before the first board.
- **Brand-new user, Google path.** About 8 taps.
- **Returning user.** Splash → Home → "עוד סיבוב" is 1 tap (HomeScreen.tsx:126-133). A fresh choice is 3 taps, 4 against a bot.
- **Staged practice from Home.** "שחק" → Modes row 6 → map → Play is 3 taps plus the 2 s "מוכן?". Home never mentions it.

Other findings:

- **Results loop.** Ranked "משחק חדש" searches again at once (app/results/[id].tsx:48-58). Practice goes back to GameType (line 61), which costs 2 more taps for solo and 3 for bot. A friends game goes to /modes, and the room is lost (line 60).
- **Teaching.** No onboarding for the game's unique rules. The only teaching is 4 splash tips shown while the app loads (SplashScreen.tsx:16-21), plus "איך משחקים", which exists only for staged practice (screens/levels/HowToPlay.tsx). There is no help route at all.
- **Home recent list.** It shows practices only (RecentGames.tsx:41), but the design board shows ranked games there (Dir-C-Home.dc.html).
- **Coming soon.** The Achievements tab shows "בקרוב" (ProgressScreen.tsx:134-141).
- **Settings.** Lean (SettingsScreen.tsx:71-132), but it has no help or contact entry.
lanes.verdictOnMosheFeedback:
I agree with Moshe's stance (improve what exists rather than add features, because the app already has many options). In this lane the real gains are flow polish, not new screens.

- **The option count is already high.** Modes offers 8 tappable choices (6 rows in homeModel.ts:46-53, plus the 2 friends buttons at ModesScreen.tsx:288-340), above the original's "five options only" (§5; Moshe approved the extras in D48 and D80a). So I propose no new entry point on Modes.
- **What to do instead:** lower the decision density (UX-8: jargon, "unrated" repeated many times) and add shortcuts that skip decisions:
  - first-game row on Home (UX-1c)
  - one-tap "משחק חדש" on Results (UX-2)
  - continue-stages row on Home (UX-4)
- **Only three items are new:**
  - the rules card (UX-1): new content on the existing HowToPlay shell, no new game rule
  - D89 (UX-10): already approved by him
  - D24 (UX-11): conflicts with the original and needs his yes
- **His visual ideas** (a background of moving digits, digit-character avatars) belong to other lanes. One UX caveat from this lane: a moving background should stay off the game screen and the forms (Login and Register), and needs his eyes on the device.

proposals.title: Teach the 4 unique rules once, and give a new player a one-tap first game
proposals.problem:
The rules that make this game different are never taught before or during a normal game: a cell locks to you for 8/12/18 s, harder moves score more, a mistake costs what the right digit would have scored, and interferences cost points.

- **Splash tips only.** The only teaching is 4 rotating tips (SplashScreen.tsx:16-21: TIPS lock/hard/mistake/interfere, TIP_MS=4000). They show only while sign-in loads, and spec §22 wants the app open in under 2 s, so a player sees at most one tip.
- **Staged practice only.** "איך משחקים" exists only there (screens/levels/HowToPlay.tsx:22-31, used nowhere else).
- **No help anywhere.** apps/mobile/app has no help route, Settings has no help row (SettingsScreen.tsx:71-132), and the interferences guide opens only from the Achievements tab (app/achievements.tsx:39).
- **Unexplained label.** GameType shows "זמן למשבצת" (home.json:175; GameTypeScreen.tsx:175) without saying what a lock is.
- **No starting point.** For a brand-new player lastPlayOf returns null (homeModel.ts:241-245), so the "עוד סיבוב" row is hidden (HomeScreen.tsx:198). They face 6 rows + 2 buttons on Modes with no suggestion, and the default type is 'normal' (homeModel.ts:119).
proposals.proposal:
(a) **"How Sudoku Fight works" card.** Reuse the HowToPlay shell, with pictures drawn from the real board as HowToPlayPanels does:
1. Tap a cell: it is yours for N s (N from the rules); pick a digit.
2. A harder move is worth more points.
3. A mistake costs exactly the points of the right digit.
4. Versus only: spend points on an interference in two taps.

Buttons "הבנתי" and "דלג". Show it once per phone, before the first solo, bot, ranked or friends game; keep the seen flag the way useTutorials does. Reuse the splash tip copy (account.json splash.tips.*) so the numbers stay rule-driven.

proposals.title: Home tells one story: recent games include ranked, and the card's numbers match

proposals.title: No "בקרוב" in a main tab at launch

proposals.title: Show what a game earned on Results: XP, level bar, level-up and the interference it unlocks
proposals.problem:
- **Built but invisible.** XP and levels are in V1 (spec §15), and levels 2, 3 and 4 each unlock an interference (D17, D47). Yet Results for solo, bot, ranked and friends shows no XP and no level bar: nothing in screens/results mentions XP.

- When the bar crosses a level: "רמה 3!", the unlocked interference's TokenArt ("נפתחה: חתולים") and a link to the interferences guide.

evidence: docs/01-SPEC.md:1382-1391 (§15 XP, levels, interference unlocks at levels 2, 3, 4)
proposals.reducedMotionAndPerf: The bar fills over about 600 ms with the existing tokens. Under Reduced Motion it jumps to its final width, and the level badge appears without the pop, as the rating counter already does. Cheap: one Reanimated width value.

proposals.title: First launch speaks to a new player, and an invited friend sees the invite
proposals.problem:
- **Wrong audience.** A fresh install opens on Login, whose title and subtitle speak to a returning player: "חוזרים לזירה" / "הדירוג, הרצף והיריבים שלך מחכים" (account.json:90-92). The primary button is "התחברות", and sign-up is a small link, "אין לך משתמש? הרשמה" (LoginScreen.tsx:97-112).

- **Long email path.** About 11 taps and 4 typed fields before the first board, including a confirm-password field even though the field has a show-password eye (RegisterAccountScreen.tsx:66, :85).
proposals.proposal:
1. **Welcome variant.** When this phone has never had a signed-in account (a stored flag), Login shows "ברוכים הבאים לזירה", the splash tagline ("לוח אחד. כולם פותרים. רק אחד מנצח."), the primary button "צור לוחם" (→ /register/fighter), Google, and a secondary "כבר יש לי חשבון" that reveals the email form. Phones that have signed in before keep today's screen.

proposals.title: One copy-and-density pass: plain words, each fact said once
proposals.problem:
- **Jargon.** The GameType cards say "נפתר בבודד גלוי בלבד", "דורש בודד נסתר" and "דורש זוגות או צמצומים" (home.json:145, :150, :155; shown at GameTypeScreen.tsx:223). These terms mean nothing to most players.

- **Implementation details as notes.** "הלוח נבחר מהלוחות שבמכשיר, בלי לחזור על לוח ששיחקת לאחרונה" (home.json:161), and a 3-sentence think-time paragraph on BotSelect (home.json:251).

proposals.proposal:
- Rewrite the technique lines as what the player experiences: "למתחילים", "צריך לחפש לאן ספרה יכולה להיכנס", "למתקדמים". Keep the technique names in the accessibility label.

- Put the radio in the same place on both screens.

proposals.title: Tell an unverified player before they choose ranked, not after

proposals.title: D24 re-raised: let a new player practise before signing up
proposals.problem:
Every signed-out player is sent to /login, whatever screen they ask for (auth/redirect.ts:84-89). A first board costs about 8 taps (Google) or 11 taps plus 4 typed fields (email). The app already has most of what guest practice needs:

Presented for decision, because it conflicts with the original.

lanes.lane: BRD: core play surface (board, cells, keypad, game-screen layout) and accessibility
lanes.currentState:
Input is cell-first by design. You tap an empty cell, it shows a pending ring, the server locks it, the keypad arms, and the digit is judged at once (spec 01-SPEC.md:858-883). Wrong digits never stay in the cell: they become small red marks, and the last 3 are shown (boardModel.ts:338-343). Because of that, there is no conflict display, no erase and no undo. The spec agrees: notes and erase are not in V1 (01-SPEC.md:878-879).

Keypad (Keypad.tsx):
- Always a single LTR row with a remaining count under each digit.
- A digit already tried wrongly in this cell is struck in red [D12]; a digit with all 9 placed is dimmed.
- An idle press nudges the lock strip (GameScreen.tsx:1259-1262).
- "ביטול בחירה" is a ghost button under the keypad (CancelSelection.tsx).

Board (Board.tsx, Cell.tsx):
- Draws all 14 cell states, with fixed corners: owner glyph, seconds pill, wrong digits.
- My lock has a ring, a 1 dp contrast edge, a pulse and a seconds pill. An opponent's lock has a ring and their mini avatar.
- A solved cell has its owner's tint plus a 6 dp design glyph (● ▲ ■ ◆).
- Correct, wrong and taken flashes all have Reduced Motion versions. The outer cells' touch area reaches 44 dp (geometry.ts:65-70).
- There is no row/column/box highlight and no same-digit highlight (components.md:527, 791), and the coordinate rails are off.

Layout: a single column. The board side is min(width − 32, measured room) (screens/game/geometry.ts:53-57). The keypad takes the same width as the board (GameScreen.tsx:1513-1518). Portrait only (app.json:7), with supportsTablet false (app.json:13).

Accessibility:
- Every cell has a label and a hint (labels.ts).
- An invisible live region speaks at most once every 1.5 s (useLiveAnnouncer.ts). The lock strip speaks on lock, at 3 s and on release (LockStrip.tsx:138-154).
- Colour contrast is tested from the tokens (src/__tests__/contrast.test.ts).
- Reduced Motion follows the system plus an in-app setting (theme/motion.ts:13-17).
- Signed numbers and cell names get LRI/PDI isolates through ltr() and signedText() (components/player/format.ts).
- Gap: maxFontSizeMultiplier is used nowhere in the app (grep finds none), and there is no layout test for short screens (model.test.ts:143-146 only checks widths).

Not recommended:
- Digit-first input. It skips the visible lock, which conflicts with original §11 and with 01-SPEC.md:879 ("entry only with an active lock").
- Auto-candidates, or dimming keys that already appear in the row/column/box. That would solve the puzzle for the player, against 01-SPEC.md:80 ("fair sudoku solving is the core").
- Notes. They would need a second, non-locking input mode inside 8–18 s locks. Leave them out of the store release.
lanes.verdictOnMosheFeedback:
I partly agree. On the play surface the polish gap is real:
- No feedback at the big moments: a row, column or box completed, or the 9th of a digit placed.
- The board-reveal motion was designed but never built: tokens.json:936-941 and motion.md:334 define it, and no code uses those values.
- The keypad keys are flat, unlike the CTA.

BRD-7, BRD-8 and BRD-9 fix these without touching the rules.

Two warnings for this lane:

(1) Drifting background digits. They are fine on menus. On the game screen they must not move near the board. 01-SPEC.md:73 says "הלוח תמיד קריא… אנימציות ואפקטים לא פוגעים בריכוז". Digits 1–9 floating beside a sudoku grid during an 8–18 s lock compete with the real digits, so freeze or hide them while a game runs, and make them static under Reduced Motion.

(2) Number-character avatars. An opponent's avatar is drawn in the centre of the empty cell they lock, exactly where a digit goes (Cell.tsx:315-317; components.md §11.3 #6). It is 22 dp at the design size and about 20 dp on a 360 dp phone. A "7 pirate" there reads as a placed 7. The scramble interference also paints fake digits in the sender's colour (spec 01-SPEC.md, section 7.1), which would deepen the confusion. If Moshe chooses digit characters, the in-cell mini avatar needs one of these:
- a face crop that hides the digit's outline;
- the seat glyph in a disc of the player's ring colour.

Moshe needs to check this on the device.

proposals.title: A digit pressed while my tap is still waiting for the server goes to the wrong place or is lost
proposals.problem:
Online, a tap on a cell only marks it pending. The keypad arms only once the server confirms the lock (packages/engine/src/game/view.ts:283-287; boardModel.ts:304-318), and onDigit always targets the confirmed lock (GameScreen.tsx:1251-1258).

(a) First lock: within the round trip (about 80–200 ms) the keypad is idle. A fast cell-then-digit press only shakes "בחר משבצת" (GameScreen.tsx:1259-1262; Keypad.tsx:255-259), and the digit is dropped.

(b) Switching from cell A to B: the keypad is still armed for A, so the digit is sent as place(A). If the server refuses B (taken, or the 1 s re-lock wait), A stays locked (engine.ts:731-741 rejects before releasing A). place(A) is then accepted (engine.ts:751-760), so a digit meant for B lands in A and can cost a penalty. If B succeeds, place(A) is rejected as notLockedCell, and the screen says nothing (GameScreen.tsx:960-966 only reacts to 'cooldown').
proposals.proposal:
Bind each press to the cell the player sees as selected.
- While a select is pending, the keypad is armed for the pending cell, not the old lock.
  - Its tried digits come from view.wrong[pending]; its complete digits from view.keypad.remaining.
- onDigit sends place(shownPending ?? myLock.cell, d). Messages go in order on one socket (remoteGameHost.ts:651-661), so the server runs select(B) before place(B, d):
  - lock granted: the digit is judged as usual;
  - lock refused: place(B) is rejected with no penalty, and the existing 'taken'/'cooldown' shake explains why.
  - The rate limits allow it: select 10/s, place 5/s (apps/server/src/game/gate.ts:26-29).
- No idle nudge while a select is pending.
- Optional: after a press, show the digit faintly with the pending ring until the answer. That is not a result, so it fits 01-SPEC.md:1587.
- Jest tests:
  - remote host: a press during a pending select sends place for the pending cell;
  - GameScreen: a press during a switch never targets the old lock;
  - LocalGameHost is unchanged, since its select is synchronous.
evidence: packages/engine/src/game/view.ts:283-287 (keypad enabled only with a confirmed lock)
apps/mobile/src/net/remoteGameHost.ts:651-661 (select only sets pending; nothing applied locally)
packages/engine/src/game/engine.ts:731-741 (refused select keeps the old lock), 751-760 (place targets the lock cell)

proposals.title: Short phones: the board and keypad shrink together; add a compact layout and decouple the keypad
proposals.proposal:
(1) Keypad width = min(window width − 2×gutter, about 520), independent of the board. On a 360 phone, keys stay ≥ 33 dp wide even when the board is short.

(2) Compact rhythm when the measured room is under about 300 dp:
- gaps 16/20/16/12 → 8/8/4/4 (saves about 40 dp);
- "ביטול בחירה" moves to the end of the lock-strip row as an icon+label pill. Keep the draining bar there, shortened, as spec §6.2.8 requires. This saves about 60 dp.
- Original §12 lists "מחיקה / ביטול" as part of the keypad area, so a cancel near the input is consistent.

(3) Jest layout tests at 360×640, 360×740 with a 48 dp nav bar, and 411×731 at fontScale 1.3. Assert board ≥ 300 dp (≥ 260 at 640) and key width ≥ 30 dp.

(4) If it is still short after this, then consider a shorter 2P card variant. That one needs design.
proposals.specConflict: Design doc only: components.md §12.2 places cancel centred under the keypad. Moving it in compact mode needs Moshe's OK. Nothing in the original spec conflicts.

proposals.title: Large system text breaks the board and keypad: set a font-scale policy for the play surface
proposals.problem:
No Text in the app caps font scaling (grep finds no maxFontSizeMultiplier), and text() adds none (theme/index.ts:54-68). The cell digits, wrong-digit marks, seconds pill and key digit/count are all sized to fixed geometry:
- Cell.tsx:488-496, 325-340, 757-769; Keypad.tsx:308-316.
- The cell clips its content (overflow hidden, Cell.tsx:993-998), so at large iOS text sizes (Larger Text goes up to about 3×) or Android 200%, digits are cut.
- The key's content (32 + 12 dp text) spills out of its 60 dp height from about 1.5×.
- The lock strip has a fixed 24 dp height (LockStrip.tsx:169-175).
The 9×9 board cannot grow with the text, so the system scale only damages it.
proposals.proposal:
Add a scale prop to ui/Text: 'board' caps at 1.0, 'hud' caps at about 1.35. Use it like this:
- 'board': cell digits, wrong digits, seconds pill, key digit and count.
- 'hud': lock strip, scores and names on the game cards. Fixed-height rows get numberOfLines={1} with adjustsFontSizeToFit.

Give large-text users a real gain inside the cell: when fontScale ≥ 1.15, raise the digit from about 0.57 to about 0.66 of the cell (Rubik 22 → 25 at the design's 38.4 dp), and wrong digits from 11 to 12.

Add a Jest check that Cell and Keypad text carries the cap.
evidence: grep: no maxFontSizeMultiplier in apps/mobile/src or app

proposals.title: Screen readers cannot finish a move inside the lock time; filled cells read as disabled buttons
proposals.problem:
With TalkBack or VoiceOver you lock a cell, then must swipe past every remaining cell to reach the keypad, because the keypad comes after the board in the reading order (GameScreen.tsx:1486-1524). The lock lasts 8, 12 or 18 s (packages/engine/src/game/rules.ts:67), and from cell A1 there are up to 80 cells to pass.

Every given or solved cell is a button marked disabled (Cell.tsx:250-263), so the reader says "button, disabled" on most of the 81 cells.

On iOS, the live region and the lock strip each call announceForAccessibility. A new announcement cuts off the one still being read (useLiveAnnouncer.ts:30; LockStrip.tsx:145-153).

(1) On my locked cell, add accessibilityActions with one action per armed digit ("הזן 5" / "Enter 5") plus "ביטול בחירה". onAccessibilityAction calls the same onDigit/onCancel that Board receives from GameScreen. proposals.title: The owner glyph is about 5 dp on a 360 dp phone, too small to carry ownership for colour-blind players
proposals.problem:
The glyph is 6 dp at the design's 38.4 dp cell (tokens.json:835-838, Cell.tsx:533-543). Scaled and rounded with px(), it is 5 dp on a 328 dp board (a 360 dp phone) and 5 dp at 312 dp. At that size ● ◆ ■ ▲ are hard to tell apart.

The glyph is painted in the digit colour. In a protanopia simulation (Machado 2009 model), the P2 and P3 digit/glyph colours (#9a4a0c vs #256412) differ by ΔE ≈ 2.7, so they look the same, and the shape alone must carry ownership. The P1 tint vs the alternate cell colour (cellAlt) is ΔE ≈ 3.1 in the same simulation.

Spec §22 and CLAUDE.md require shapes so ownership never depends on colour alone; original §11 asks that the owner be very clear with 3–4 players.

Raise size.solverGlyph from 6 to 9 design dp (7–8 dp on a 360 phone), keeping it at the top-left at inset 3. The corner is free: the pill is top-right, wrong digits bottom-right, and the digit is centred.

Add a 1 dp outline in the cell colour so the shape stands out from the tint.

Check on the device in a 4-player game, with a colour-blind filter (Android developer options: Simulate colour space).

proposals.title: Scan aids allowed by the rules: same-digit peek and the pending peer highlight
proposals.problem:
In a game, a tap on a given or solved cell does nothing: it is not interactive (boardModel.ts:255-271) and the Pressable has no onPress (Cell.tsx:256-259). Players scan by eye for every placement.

The board already has a target-chip look used by find stages (boardModel.ts:163-164, 268; Cell.tsx:546-571).

The peer highlight is still open point #6 for Moshe (components.md:527, 791), with a neutral #dfe3ec proposed.
proposals.proposal:
(a) Same-digit peek: a tap on a filled cell highlights every cell with that digit (a light outline and a bolder digit) for about 3 s or until the next tap. It is local only, with no host call.

(b) Peer highlight: when I hold a lock, its row, column and box get the neutral #dfe3ec under the cell content. Solved cells keep their tint.

Both go behind a config flag (`boardAids` in config) so Moshe can switch each one.

Fairness:
- They show only what is already on the board, the same for everyone.
- Both are off during a scramble or ink hit on me; otherwise they would defeat it (spec §7.1).
- Both are off in staged practice: tap stages take taps on filled cells, and find stages already show target chips.

Explicitly not proposed: auto-candidates, or dimming keys that already appear in the row/column/box. They solve for the player (01-SPEC.md:80).
proposals.specConflict: None with the original spec. Peer highlight is open point #6 in components.md §17, still waiting for Moshe's approval.

proposals.title: Feel the big moments: row, column and box completion, and the 9th of a digit
proposals.problem:
Completing a row, column or box, or placing the last of a digit, gets nothing beyond the normal correct flash. grep finds no completion handling in the board, the game screen or motion.md.

The key of a completed digit jumps to opacity .3 in one render (Keypad.tsx:301-302).

The data is already in hand: the 'correct' effect carries the move's breakdown (game/effects.ts:26; MoveScore row/col/box/num, scoring.ts:34-42). row === 8 means the move completed that row; num === 8 means the digit is complete.
proposals.proposal:
On a correct move:
- For each completed unit, a 350–450 ms light sweep across it in the solver's ring colour at ≤ 25% opacity, under the digits. Several units at once are staggered by 60 ms.
- For a completed digit, its keypad key plays a short check pop and settles into the complete look.
- It works for every player's moves, each in that player's colour.

Stay short so the board stays readable (01-SPEC.md:73). Add the new effects to reducedMotion.test.ts.
evidence: docs/01-SPEC.md:73, 75 (every significant state change felt; board always readable)

Performance: one absolutely positioned View per completed unit (at most 3 at once), animating opacity/translateX on the UI thread with shared values. No Reanimated layout animations, per noLayoutAnimationsInGame.test.ts.

proposals.title: Build the game-start reveal that the design already times

proposals.problem: Keys are flat: a background, a 1 dp border and a radius (Keypad.tsx:328-341). proposals.title: Android 16 tablets and foldables will ignore the portrait lock: mark the app as a game
proposals.problem: The app is portrait only (app.json:7; AndroidManifest.xml:21), and its layout is a single column. It targets SDK 36 (React Native's libs.versions.toml:4, which the Expo root plugin uses as the default). For apps targeting 36, Android 16 ignores orientation and resizability limits on screens 600 dp wide and up (tablets, unfolded foldables). Games marked with android:appCategory="game" are exempt. The manifest and plugins set no appCategory (grep finds none). In landscape on a tablet, the board would shrink to about 330 dp between wide rows of cards.
proposals.proposal: Add a small config plugin, next to withAppLocales.js, that sets android:appCategory="game" on <application>. Portrait then stays enforced on large screens, and the system also classes the app as a game. Check on a foldable or tablet in Google Play's pre-launch report (the local emulator cannot run). A real wide layout (board beside the cards and keypad) can come later if Moshe wants tablets.

lanes.lane: Launch quality and first impression in the store

The groundwork is solid; the gaps are about polish and launch timing. TIME-CRITICAL: the domain decision (LCH-10) must be made before plan step 7, the first production AAB, because that build fixes the host for room links.

- Crashlytics: wired. Lazy module started at auth init (auth/index.ts:20), error boundary (_layout.tsx:119), Hermes rejection tracker (crashlytics.ts). Firebase Analytics and our own telemetry send funnel events (protocol telemetry.ts:37-79). Sentry is on the server only.
- Cold start: fonts are embedded on Android release, auth opens from the cached profile (authStore.ts:178-182), and background work waits for the first screen (_layout.tsx:43, PERF.md). No release measurement on a real device is recorded.

- Legal: privacy, terms and delete-account pages exist in 19 languages on the server (apps/server/src/legal). Account deletion works in the app. IARC and Data safety answers are prepared. The script for deletion requests by email is deferred (plan.md "not now").

proposals.title: Harden the store build: R8 and resource shrinking, native and JS symbols, Crashlytics attributes
proposals.problem:

1. R8 is off (android/app/build.gradle:69, default false). There is no deobfuscation mapping and no native debug symbols; the audit already noted the Play warnings. debugSymbolLevel is set nowhere.
2. Crashlytics shows Hermes JS frames as bundle offsets, and no source map is kept per build (eas.json has no buildArtifactPaths).
3. Staging and production share one Firebase project (FIREBASE-SETUP.md:163), and the reporter sets no attributes (its interface has only recordError, setUser and log; crashlytics.ts:28-33). Staging crashes mix with production, and you can't filter by language (19) or environment.

Size, from the local arm64-only release APK (73.6 MB):
- 6 dex files: 61 MB raw, 22 MB compressed.
- JS bundle: 9.6 MB, up from 5.76 MB in PERF.md before the 17 new languages; the locales alone are 3.2 MB of JSON.

- CrashReporter calls setAttributes({ env: EXPO_PUBLIC_SERVER_LABEL, lang, version }) at start and on every language change.
- In eas.json production, add buildArtifactPaths for the Hermes source map (android/app/build/generated/sourcemaps/react/release/*.map). Add scripts/symbolicate.mjs, reusing bundle-report.mjs's source-map reader, to turn a Crashlytics frame into file:line.
- appConfig.test.ts checks the flags are set only in store builds.
- Smoke-test the R8 build on a phone (sign-in, Google, ranked, interferences, sqlite, language switch), and compare Play's App size report before and after.

proposals.title: An update strategy for day 2: a server version gate and JS hotfixes over the air
proposals.problem:
After launch there is no way to tell a player to update:

- A protocol mismatch ends in a generic 'refused' error (remoteGameHost.ts:854-857, then connectionStatus.ts:67-68).

Over-the-air updates are off: app.json has no updates.url or runtimeVersion (the audit found ENABLED=false), and RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:224 says to answer 'no' to EAS Update.

(1) Server endpoint GET /v1/app-config, or new fields in /health: {minVersion, latestVersion, openQueues?}. The app reads it after the first screen (useAfterFirstScreen):
- Older than latest: a dismissible Home banner, 'New version available', with the Play or App Store link.
- Older than min: a blocking screen with the store button. This doubles as a kill switch for a broken build.
All text goes through t().

(2) EAS Update, for JS and text hotfixes only: updates.url, runtimeVersion { policy: 'fingerprint' }, a channel per eas.json profile, checkAutomatically: 'ON_LOAD' and fallbackToCacheTimeout: 0. Cold start never waits; an update applies on the next launch. expo-updates already ships, so its size is already paid (LCH-6).

(3) RELEASE-CHECKLIST says when an OTA is allowed: JS only, same runtime, staging first.

evals.idea: Moshe's proposal: replace the flat dark background with faint animated digits that wander the screen (walk, hop, stop, look around). Very faint, but visible.
evals.currentState:
Background today:
- No shared Screen wrapper. The root paints color.bg (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:67), the Stack contentStyle paints it again (_layout.tsx:77), and about 40 screens each paint their own root `{ flex: 1, backgroundColor: color.bg }`. Examples: HomeScreen.tsx:299, ResultsScreen.tsx:492, SearchView.tsx:305, GameScreen.tsx:1684, account/parts.tsx:343.
- So a background behind the Stack would be hidden. It has to be mounted per screen, as an absolute sibling under that screen's content. On Home that means under the ScrollView (HomeScreen.tsx:138-139), so it does not scroll.
- color.bg is #0f1218, surface #171b24, textMuted #9aa3b5, textFaint #828ba1 (tokens.generated.ts:18-24). textFaint, at 5.50:1 on bg, is the tightest text token.

Where the background would actually show on Home:
- ProfileCard is an opaque surface with no border (ProfileCard.tsx:235-239).
- The hero button is opaque gold. BottomNav is opaque nav.bg (BottomNav.tsx:74).
- Recent-game rows are transparent, with only a hairline border (RecentGames.tsx:168-179). Their text sits directly on bg, so digits would pass behind it.

Motion rules today:
- motion.md:30-33 (§1.4): "Only functional loops… Round 1's decorative idle loops are dropped". motion.md:58 lists the dropped sf-bob, sf-twinkle, sf-sway and so on. motion.md:37: "Premium comes from timing, not effects".
- Spec §1 (01-SPEC.md:73): "the board is always readable; animations don't hurt concentration".
- The original spec asks for Gaming Premium, depth and animations "as part of the experience" (00-original-spec-v1.md:54-70).

Startup and performance constraints:
- Skia is deliberately kept out of the startup path (startupGraph.test.ts:16 LATE_PACKAGES; PERF.md:166-169), and Home is the first screen.
- Home stays mounted under the game (useScreenFocused.ts:5-6). AvatarArt already pauses on blur (AvatarArt.tsx:141-145).
- The screen is kept on in the foreground on every screen (config/display.ts:11). A Home left open would animate forever.
- Spec §22: at least 55fps in Release on a mid Android, and open in under 2 s.

Existing patterns to reuse:
- One frame clock: useFrameCallback with setActive (hitClock.ts:57-79).
- One Skia picture recorded on the UI thread per frame (Scramble.tsx:59-117, 147-150), with a Jest Skia mock (interference/testing/skiaMock.ts).
- A deterministic hash instead of Math.random (Confetti.tsx:35-41).
- Reduced Motion is the app setting system/on/off (theme/motion.ts:13-17, settings.ts:41,59).
- No Skia font is used anywhere. gen-icons.mjs:10-12 already pulls Rubik digit outlines out of the font into paths (scripts/lib/ttf.mjs).
- Avatar digit characters 0-9 exist, with outline paths (packages/avatars/src/catalog/digits.ts:1-9, 140, 196, 627).
- Avatar idle on Home is off: AVATAR_STAGES.home=false (avatars/reactions.ts:222, used at ProfileCard.tsx:128). Decision 3.19 is still open (DECISIONS-PENDING.md:665-671).
- The competitive Results screen has no win confetti, although motion.md §4.7 specifies it ("confetti | Win only, + 700 | 1600") and tokens have victory.confetti 1600 (tokens.generated.ts:906). Confetti is used only in LevelResultView.tsx:278; ResultsScreen.tsx:11 imports only Button and Spinner.
evals.verdict:
Do it, with changes. It is a good fit for the "Gaming Premium, depth, alive" goal (original spec §2), and it is cheap at runtime if built as one Skia canvas. It must stay inside these limits:

1. Only on calm, low-text screens: Home first, then Login/Register and the Match Search wait.
2. Never on any screen with a board or keypad, never on the 3-2-1 countdown, and never on number-heavy lists (History, Leaderboard).
3. Calm by design:
   - Neutral grey ink at about 7% (precomposited to a solid colour).
   - Nine digits, with at least half of them resting at any moment.
   - Slow walking (≤12 dp/s).
   - Everything settles and the clock stops after 25 s without touch (the screen is kept on).
4. Reduced Motion: one static frame.
5. Skia is loaded lazily after the first screen, so the under-2-s start and the startup-graph test hold.
6. It contradicts motion.md §1.4, which is a design-doc rule written after round 1's "too colorful" feedback. It is not an original-spec rule, so Moshe can change it, but it must be his explicit decision, recorded as a new D-number.

Do the cheaper "alive" items next to it: the spec'd win confetti on Results, which is missing, and avatar idle on Home (3.19). The final faintness needs Moshe's eyes on his phone.
pros: Answers the original spec directly (00-original-spec-v1.md:54-70: Gaming Premium, visual depth, animations as part of the experience). Today Home is a flat #0f1218 with no motion at rest.

Uses the game's own symbol, the digits 1-9, so it reads as sudoku identity rather than generic decoration. It ties to the app icon, which already uses faint white-at-7% grid lines (tokens.generated.ts brand.grid rgba(255,255,255,0.07)), and to the avatar digit cast.
Very low runtime cost when done as one Skia picture: 9 paths and no React renders per frame. The same pattern Scramble already ships on the game screen.
Contrast stays compliant when the ink is a precomposited solid. textMuted at 7% gives #191c23, and textFaint on it is still 5.00:1. The worst case is still above 4.5:1 (see extra).
It makes the store screenshots and first impression richer. Even as a static frame (Reduced Motion, or settled) it adds texture to a flat background.

Most of the infrastructure exists: frame clock with setActive (hitClock.ts), picture recording (Scramble.tsx), Skia Jest mock, deterministic hash (Confetti.tsx), focus hook (useScreenFocused.ts), idle deferral (services/startup.ts whenIdle), and font-to-path extraction (scripts/lib/ttf.mjs).
It can carry the avatar story if avatars become digit characters: the background extras can be faceless silhouettes of the same cast.
risks: Design rule conflict: motion.md:30-33 (§1.4) allows only functional loops, and motion.md:58 records that decorative idle loops were dropped after round 1 was judged 'too colorful and unclear' (03-DESIGN.md:121). Without care, this re-opens that exact feedback. Mitigation: neutral grey only (never seat colours or gold), at least 50% of digits resting, slow speeds, and settle after 25 s. Needs Moshe's explicit OK and a motion.md amendment.

Gameplay frame budget: Home stays mounted under the game (useScreenFocused.ts:5-6). If the clock does not stop on blur, the Home canvas keeps recording pictures on the UI thread during every game, which threatens spec §22's 55fps exactly where it matters. Pausing on blur and on AppState is mandatory and needs a test.

Battery and heat: keepScreenOn is true on every screen (display.ts:11), so a phone left on Home would animate for hours. Mitigation: settle and stop after 25 s without touch, plus 30 Hz throttling and zero updates while all digits rest.

Startup: Skia is banned from the startup graph (startupGraph.test.ts:16, PERF.md:166). Importing it from HomeScreen breaks the test and the under-2-s start. It must be required inside a function after the first screen (whenIdle), and the digits fade in about 0.3-1 s after Home appears.

Card merge artifact: filled ink at textMuted 7% (#191c23) has 1.011:1 contrast with surface #171b24, so it is visually identical. Where a digit slides under the borderless ProfileCard (ProfileCard.tsx:235-239), the card's edge would appear to grow a lump. Mitigation: give ProfileCard a hairline color.border, as RowButton and the recent rows already have, or use the outline digit style.

Readability: digits move behind the transparent recent-game rows (RecentGames.tsx:168-179), so motion sits behind text. The contrast numbers pass, but slow speed and Reduced Motion as the stop mechanism are what satisfy WCAG 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide).

Device variance: a 1.10:1 ink-to-background step can disappear on OLED panels at low brightness (black crush) or look stronger on LCD in a dark room. This needs Moshe's eyes on his phone, ideally with a dev-only tuning screen.
Overlap stacking: drawn with real alpha, two overlapping white 6% digits drop textFaint to 4.10:1. Mitigation: draw solid precomposited ink (no alpha), so overlaps never accumulate.
Scope creep: personality behaviours (hop, look, line-up) invite endless tuning. Cap the behaviour set and keep it in config.
Two canvases during transitions, if it is placed on consecutive stack screens (Home to Modes). Avoid this by keeping it off Modes, GameType and BotSelect.

designVariants.name: A. Wanderers with personality (Moshe's literal idea, recommended)
designVariants.description:
The digits 1-9, one of each (a sudoku nod), behave like small creatures behind the content.

Behaviours (a per-digit state machine on a deterministic hash):
- walk: drift along a gentle curve, with a waddle (±4° rotation and a 1.5 dp bob, 2 steps/s).
- pause: still.
- hop: a parabolic jump with squash on take-off and landing, the avatars' squash idea.
- look around: tilt -7°, hold 300 ms, +7°, back.
- spin: rare.

Light personality per digit, matching Moshe's pirate example: 1 is springy and hops more; 8 is old, rests longer and walks slowest; 7 leans forward when walking. Digits pass behind cards and are cut by their edges, which creates natural peek-in moments.

Caps: at most 1 hop at a time; at most 1 spin per 30 s per screen; at most 4 digits walking at once; at least 50% resting.

After 25 s without touch, each digit finishes its action, rests, and the clock stops. A touch or scroll wakes them.
designVariants.numbers:
- Count: 9 (7 on screens under 700 dp tall).
- Size: 3 classes, 44 / 56 / 72 dp glyph height. Rubik Bold outlines (the board's digit font), or the avatar digit silhouettes.
- Ink: solid #191c23 (textMuted at 7% over bg; 1.10:1 against bg, the same step as a card surface). Config range 5-9%.
- Walk: 8-12 dp/s, so about 40 s to cross a 393 dp screen.
- Walk spells 3-8 s. Rests 2-6 s.
- Hop: 14-18 dp high, 420 ms. Squash scaleY 0.90 / scaleX 1.08 for 80 ms.
- Look-around: 1100 ms.
- Spin: 360° in 1200 ms.
- Picture updates: 0 Hz while all rest, 30 Hz while walking, 60 Hz only during a hop or spin.
- Fade-in on first mount: 600 ms.

designVariants.name: B. Wanderers plus a 'sudoku moment' (A with a payoff)
designVariants.description:
Same as A. On top of it:
- Once per Home visit, after 12-20 s of focus, or immediately when Home is entered right after a win, the nine digits glide into a 1x9 row (a fixed valid permutation) in the largest open band: under the content, or the header band.
- They brighten slightly, hold, and wander off.
- It is a quiet echo of the game and a reward beat. Never more than once per visit, and never while the user scrolls.
designVariants.numbers:
- Everything as in A.
- Gather: 2400 ms (spring, no overshoot beyond 4 dp).
- Hold: 1800 ms. Disperse: 2000 ms.
- Ink during the hold: #1d2128 (textMuted at 10%; textFaint 4.73:1, still passing).
- Row glyph size: 36-44 dp, pitch = glyph width + 6 dp.
- Frequency: at most 1 per visit, at most 1 per 60 s.
- Adds about 1 dev day over A.

designVariants.name: C. Slow parallax layers (calmest, closest to Calm Night)
designVariants.description:
Three depth layers of digits drift slowly upward with a soft sideways sway, wrapping from top to bottom with a deterministic re-seed. No personality, no hops.

On Home, the layers also follow the ScrollView at different fractions of the scroll offset (useAnimatedScrollHandler into a shared value), so depth responds to the finger. The scroll-linked part moves only when the user scrolls, which is the most §1.4-friendly form.

It can run scroll-only (no clock at all) as the most conservative mode.

- mid: 7 digits, 40 dp, ink #171a21 (6%), 6 dp/s, scroll factor 0.18.
- near: 2 digits, 100-120 dp, ink #15181e (4%; big shapes need less), 9 dp/s, ±4° rotation, scroll factor 0.35.

evals.technicalApproach:
Recommendation: one Skia canvas per hosting screen, driven by one Reanimated frame clock, recording one SkPicture per update. This is the same pattern as Scramble.tsx:147-150 and hitClock.ts:57-79. Do not use many Animated views.

Why not Animated views:
- 9-23 Animated.Text views would each push transform/opacity through Reanimated's props path every frame (shadow-tree commits on Fabric), and Android re-rasterizes text whose scale changes.
- One picture means one shared value per update, no React renders, and vector-cheap scale and rotation.
- Confetti.tsx uses 40 Animated views, but only for 1.6 s. A persistent background is a different budget.

Pieces:
1. Glyphs
   - Add scripts/gen-digit-paths.mjs, reusing scripts/lib/ttf.mjs as gen-icons.mjs:10-12 does. It writes src/components/ambient/digitPaths.generated.ts: SVG path strings for Rubik 700 (or 900) digits 1-9, about 10 KB, with no TTF in the bundle.
   - No Skia font loading is needed (the codebase has none).
   - Build the SkPaths once on the UI runtime (Skia.Path.MakeFromSVGString) and cache them.
   - Option: if the digit-character avatars go ahead, use the avatar silhouettes from packages/avatars/src/catalog/digits.ts. They are not exported today, only the DIGITS list at line 627.
2. Model
   - src/components/ambient/ambientModel.ts: a pure worklet, `ambientFrame(seedLayout, tMs, area) -> {x, y, rot, sx, sy, digit, size}[]`, plus `restingAll(t)` and `nextWakeAt`.
   - Deterministic hash in the style of Confetti.tsx:35-41. No Math.random and no Date.now, so it can be unit tested like scrambleModel and fireworksModel.
3. Clock
   - useFrameCallback(…, false) accumulates elapsed time only while active, so a resume continues without a jump.
   - Throttle: record a new picture only when 33 ms have passed (16 ms during a hop or spin), and skip recording entirely while restingAll. This matters on 90/120 Hz phones, where frame callbacks fire 2-4x more often.
4. Gating: frame.setActive(focused && appActive && !reduce && !idleSettled && enabled).
   - focused: useScreenFocused (avatars/useScreenFocused.ts). It is essential because Home stays under the game.
   - appActive: AppState 'active', the same pattern as services/keepAwake.ts.
   - idleSettled: 25 s since the last touch. Use onTouchStart on the screen root, which does not steal touches, plus the ScrollView's onScrollBeginDrag.
   - Reduced Motion: useReduceMotion (theme/motion.ts:13-17).
5. Draw
   - In createPicture: fill the canvas with color.bg, then for each glyph save, translate, rotate, scale, drawPath with ONE solid precomposited ink paint, and restore.
   - No alpha, so overlaps never stack and the contrast stays exactly the token value.
   - Canvas is absolute fill, pointerEvents="none", accessibilityElementsHidden, importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants".
6. Lazy loading
   - An `AmbientBackground` wrapper (React and Reanimated only; on the startup path) renders nothing for the first screen.
   - Inside whenIdle (services/startup.ts:28), it calls `require('./AmbientCanvas')` and fades the canvas in over 600 ms.
   - Add 'apps/mobile/src/components/ambient/AmbientCanvas' to LATE_FILES in startupGraph.test.ts. Skia stays in LATE_PACKAGES.
   - On later visits Skia is already loaded, because the game screen loads it.
7. Config
   - src/config/ambient.ts: { enabled, screens: { home: true, login: true, register: true, search: true, results: false, …all others false }, count, inkLevel, speeds, idleSettleMs: 25000, hz }. The screens map follows the AVATAR_STAGES pattern.
   - Tokens in docs/design/tokens.json: color.ambient.digit '#191c23', color.ambient.digitBright '#1d2128' (Variant B), and motion.ambient.* (durations, caps). Regenerate with `npm run tokens`.
8. Host placement
   - Home: an absolute sibling before the ScrollView inside styles.screen (HomeScreen.tsx:138).
   - Login/Register: account/parts.tsx screen root (line 343).
   - Search: SearchView root (line 305). Use half the count there, because the radar sweep and seat blink already loop on that screen.
9. ProfileCard: add a hairline color.border (ProfileCard.tsx:235-239) to avoid the card-merge artifact.
10. Dev-only tuning screen `/dev/ambient`, like `/dev/avatars`, with sliders for ink level, count, speed and variant, so Moshe can pick the faintness on his phone. It sits behind __DEV__, like app/dev/* (PERF.md item 3).
evals.reducedMotionAndPerf:
Reduced Motion (app setting 'on', or 'system' with the OS flag):
- One static picture: the seeded rest layout, every digit in a rest pose, same ink.
- The frame callback is never activated and there is no fade-in.
- This keeps the texture (Moshe's faint digits) with zero motion. It also gives WCAG 2.2.2 its pause/stop mechanism through the existing Settings → Motion choice (SettingsScreen.tsx:91-99).

Pausing:
- Stop on screen blur (useScreenFocused) and on any AppState other than 'active'.
- Stop on idle-settle: 25 s after the last touch, the digits finish their actions and rest, then setActive(false), so zero cost while the phone sits on Home with keepScreenOn.
- Resume from the accumulated time, with no jump.

Performance budget (verify on Moshe's phone, Release, as in PERF.md):
- UI-thread cost per recorded picture: ≤1.0 ms on a mid Android (estimate 0.3-0.6 ms for 9 paths; Variant C's 23 paths about 1 ms).
- Picture updates: 0 Hz all resting, 30 Hz walking, 60 Hz only during a hop or spin. Never tied to 90/120 Hz.
- Glyph caps: 12 for A/B, 24 for C, hard cap 24.
- GPU memory: one canvas surface, roughly 10 MB at 1080x2400 RGBA (estimate).
- Jank: `dumpsys gfxinfo` Janky frames on Home with ambient on vs off: at most 5%, and no regression above 1 point. The game screen's jank must be identical with Home mounted underneath (proves pause on blur). Perf Monitor UI fps at least 58 on Home.
- Battery: zero steady-state cost after settle. Active at most about 25 s per Home visit plus touches.

Low-end fallback, with no new dependency (expo-device and expo-battery are not installed; adding either needs a new dev build):
- Self-measure timeSincePreviousFrame in the frame callback.
- If the 90th percentile over the first 3 s is above 22 ms, drop to lite mode (half count, 20 Hz).
- If it is still above 22 ms, freeze to the static frame for the rest of the run.

Settings switch: not needed. Reduced Motion already turns it static, and Moshe does not want more options. Keep `ambientConfig.enabled` and the per-screen map in config (CLAUDE.md: decisions as config), and ask Moshe whether he wants a dedicated "animated background" switch anyway.

Placement analysis (1):
- YES, Home: the hub. Visible background is the header band, gaps, gutters and transparent recent rows; cards hide the rest.
- YES, Login/Register: first impression, space around forms.
- YES at half count, Match Search: the dead wait time. SearchView already has the radar sweep and seat blink loops (SearchView.tsx:219-245), so lower intensity there.
- NO, Game screen and all game-like screens (GameScreen, TapLevel, PuzzleLevel, Replay):
  - Spec §1 (01-SPEC.md:73) says the board is always readable, and motion.md:24-26 says "Motion never hides the board", "stay quiet inside it".
  - The board cells are opaque light (#f7f8fa), so digits would not show inside the board. They would move in the HUD, in the gaps between keypad keys, and around the cards. Peripheral motion competes with concentration, and digit shapes drifting between the keypad keys read like keys.
- NO, 3-2-1 countdown: big digits there carry meaning.
- NO, History and Leaderboard: numbers floating behind tables of scores and ratings is the worst readability mix.
- NO, Settings, legal text and long forms: reading screens.
- NO, Levels map: it already has its 'only loop', the node pulse (motion.md §4.11).
- NO, Modes, GameType, BotSelect: dense cards, and two canvases would run during the stack slide.
- Results: no ambient. Use the spec'd confetti instead (do not stack effects).

D47 interference (Scramble) reasoning:
- Scramble draws rolling segment-display digits in the sender's seat colour over the board for 5 s (Scramble.tsx:119-125; spec 01-SPEC.md:970).
- The keypad interference swaps key positions every 1.5 s (01-SPEC.md:972).
- Ambient digits on the game screen would blur the signal 'digits moving in a colour means you are attacked' and hurt 'the game state is clear at every moment' (01-SPEC.md:76-77). Around the keypad they would add confusion exactly when the player hunts for the moved key.
- So the ambient is never in the game, and it must look different from interference digits: solid Rubik silhouettes in neutral grey, never segment digits, never seat colours, never gold (gold = action/CTA).

evals.verdict:
Do it, with changes.

Why it is worth doing:
- The concept fits the brand: in a sudoku game the fighters are the digits themselves.
- The timing is right: no production users, so changing ids now costs the least.
- The pipeline already supports it: a complete 1-9 family exists and passes the tests.

The candid diagnosis: the current set looks bland mostly because of two things that a re-skin would not touch.
1. Presentation:
   - In a game, avatars are 28-36 px. The most common reaction (a correct digit: smile and nod) moves the body 2.4 units, which is under 1 px at that size.
   - Below 40 px the face loses brows, cheeks and extras. No gimmick plays below 48 px.
   - The results winner is 28 px. The picker preview is 44 px. Home and profile never idle.
   - So the 208 gimmicks are practically invisible to a real user.
2. House style:
   - Flat fills, no outlines or gradients.
   - The same googly-eye face on 99 of 101 characters.
   - Geometric primitives on a flat coloured tile.

Digit characters drawn under the same rules and in the same places will look just as bland.

The changes:
- Fix presentation first. It is cheap and helps whatever set ships.
- Build a vertical slice (Pirate 1 and Pirate 7 at the new bar) and let Moshe judge it on his device before mass production.
- Make every series its own typeface plus costume, not the same 9 outlines in different hats.
- Show a face crop, not the whole digit, in the 22 px locked cell, to avoid confusion with game digits.
- Launch with 3-4 series plus the refreshed existing digits, and add series in updates (where unlocks can come in).
- Fix the cast: give every digit a job, balance genders, make 6 and 9 a mirror pair, keep the nose cartoonish (not hooked), no guns.

If "very invested" means Duolingo-level character animation, that needs a human illustrator and, for full rigs, a Rive animator. Code-authored SVG has a real quality ceiling.
pros: Brand fit: the characters ARE the sudoku digits. No mainstream sudoku app does this. It gives a recognisable identity for the store icon, screenshots and feature graphic, and natural brand moments (the 3·2·1 countdown, motion.md:192, played by the player's own series).
Series feel collectible. They match the original §35 'avatar unlocks' idea (00-original-spec-v1.md:921-934). The picker can show each series as a 3×3 sudoku box (1-9 in box order).
No skin tones, real people or gender-presentation choices for people avatars. A smaller representation and review surface than the current 12 people.
A series is a natural content unit for post-launch updates, and supports the V1.1 unlock content the spec already plans (01-SPEC.md:194).
Best possible timing: there are no production users, and the id-migration pattern is proven (LEGACY_AVATAR_MAP, server migration 0004, normalizeAvatarId: account.ts:201-270).
risks: Confusion with game digits. In an opponent-locked cell the 22 dp avatar sits in the centre of an empty cell. A whole-body digit (the 7 spans y 9.5-92, about 18 px at 22 px) is about the height of a game digit (Rubik 22 dp, about 15-16 dp lining figures), and the same cell lists wrong digits (Cell.tsx:247, 325-339). With 3-4 players, up to 3 such cells are on the board at once. Lv-Find already uses 'a digit on a rounded chip' for real digits (Cell.tsx:545-571). Milder cases: a leaderboard rank sits right next to a 28 px avatar (LeaderboardParts.tsx:118-127), and the podium step number sits under the avatar (ResultsVersus.tsx:297-299).
Sameness. If every series reuses the same 9 outlines, each series is 'the same 7 in a different hat'. That is exactly the 'same rig on everything' blandness Moshe objects to.

Small sizes:
- Costume details under about 4 units vanish at 22-28 px (STYLE.md:166-167), so two players' 7s from different series look alike in cells and compact cards.
- Digit eyes (r 5.5) are about 1.2 px radius at 22 px whole-body.

Quality ceiling. The current 101 were produced in about 3 days (catalog files dated 2026-10-11..13) with code-authored primitives, and that process gave the bland result. Doing the same faster will not meet 'very invested'.

Problems in the cast as given:
- Only 2 of 9 are female, and the women are defined by gender ('lady', 'young woman') while the men get roles.
- Three near-identical 'kids' (3, 4, 5) and two generic 'pirates' (6, 7).
- A big hooked nose can read as an ethnic caricature: keep it long, pointy or bulbous.
- Pirate guns or blades push the age rating: use spyglass, hook, map, mop.

Tension with the calm direction. Round 1 was rejected as 'too colorful', and motion.md:31-33 dropped decorative loops. More animation must stay on stages and in reactions, not as constant motion on every screen.
Scope. Infra, the rig upgrade and 3-4 series are about 4-6 weeks of work and can delay the store release.

Bots: keeping Pip, Biscuit, Mr. Hoot, Maestro and Overlord as non-digit characters needs a renderable-but-not-choosable id list. Today any id outside AVATAR_IDS draws av00 (catalog.ts:29-31, account.ts:266-270).
Unlocks need server enforcement: router.ts:202 only checks the id, and the server never looks at unlockLevel.
Translation: every new name and every series name is needed in 19 locales.
Staging testers on 1.1.0 will see av00 for new ids (matchModel.ts:131), and the server will reject their old ids on profile edit.

Performance: richer art means bigger SVG layers. They are parsed on the JS thread each time a reaction mounts LayeredArt (no cache across mounts, AvatarArt.tsx:373-376; only stills are cached, layerStack.ts:130). Every correct move in a 4-player game triggers one, so it must be measured on Moshe's phone.

PHASE 0: PRESENTATION (any avatar set)

- FighterCard preview: size 'home'.
- AvatarPopOut: an overlay anchored to the card's layout, at 72 px, for win, bigCorrect and hit. It uses AvatarArt with the same reaction.
- motionPlan(def, id, {size}): multiply translate amplitudes by clamp(48/size, 1, 2.2).
- Rig LOD: at 28-39 px keep tear, anger and zzz, enlarged and stripped of detail.
- Moshe decides 3.19.

PHASE 1: VERTICAL SLICE (decision gate)
- Pirate 1 and Pirate 7, each in two looks: current flat, and Rig-2 style (silhouette-only ink outline at 48 px and up, one rim highlight, tile radial vignette).
- Shown in preview.html and in /dev/avatars on the device, at 96/64/36/28/22 px.

PHASE 2: SERIES INFRA
- AvatarDef.series, plus a SERIES table: {id, name, order, unlockLevel, palette, typeface}.
- Ids are '<series>-<n>'.
- packages/protocol:
  - AVATAR_IDS becomes the new choosable list.
  - A RENDERABLE list adds the bot-only characters.
  - RETIRED_AVATAR_MAP maps the 101 old ids to new ones.
  - normalizeAvatarId chains: legacy av → LEGACY_AVATAR_MAP (rows unchanged) → retired map → new id.
- Server: a migration rewrites users.avatar_id (humans and personas); PERSONA_AVATAR_IDS is rebuilt from the new list; router accepts the new ids only.
- Picker: AVATAR_GROUPS by series; 3 columns in sudoku-box order; tiles up to about 96 px with 3 columns (inner width ~342), so gimmicks play in the grid.
- Also: i18n strings (gen-avatar-strings plus 19 locales), test fixtures (about 81 files reference ids, 63 of them tests), preview regeneration.

PHASE 3: RIG 2 (packages/avatars)

ITEM 4: SERIES THEMES (11 candidates)
Each series has a typeface, a palette and a signature gimmick. None uses guns, IP lookalikes or real people.

1. Pirates. Chunky wooden-slab digits with plank grain and nails. Navy, red, gold. Gimmicks: parrot, spyglass, hook, pipe puffs.
2. Castle (knights and royals). Blackletter-serif digits in stone, silver and purple. Gimmicks: visor drop, plume, jester bells, staff sparks.
3. Robots. 7-segment LCD digits with bolts and an antenna. Gimmicks: segments flicker or light in sequence (cheap with opacity keyframes), gears spin, steam vents.
4. Space crew. Rounded futuristic digits in suits and helmets. Gimmicks: zero-g float idle, jetpack puffs, visor glint.
5. Monster party. Gooey, dripping digits: vampire, mummy wraps, bolts, slime. Gimmicks: drips, bandage unravel, bat wings.
6. Kitchen brigade. Soft dough or pastry digits with toques. Gimmicks: steam, whisk spin, sprinkles.
7. Football club. Varsity block digits in jerseys: striker, goalie, referee, coach. Gimmicks: ball bounce, whistle, scarf wave.
8. Circus. Marquee digits with bulbs: ringmaster, acrobat, strongwoman, juggler. Gimmicks: bulbs chase, juggling balls.
9. Wild West. Wood-type Clarendon digits: sheriff star, cowgirl lasso. No guns. Gimmicks: lasso spin, tumbleweed, hat tip.
10. Heroes (original). Bold italic comic digits with capes and masks. Gimmicks: cape flutter, power glow.
11. Ocean friends. Bubbly digits under water (2 as a seahorse curve, 8 as a puffer). Gimmicks: bubbles, fins.

Keep the existing 0-9 as 'Originals'.

PIRATES: FULL CAST (shape → role, props, gimmick, motion)
