merged.title: Fix: a digit pressed during a pending cell switch lands in the old lock or is lost
merged.reason: Checked in the code. onDigit always sends place(board.myLock.cell) (GameScreen.tsx:1251-1258). myLock comes from the lock the server has confirmed (boardModel.ts:325-331). In the engine, a refused select keeps the old lock (engine.ts:731-741), and a place on the old lock is still judged (engine.ts:751-757). critic.viewOnBackground:
Do it, but as item 11-12 rather than top 5, and only after the tactile surface system.

The case for it:
- It is Moshe's most 'ours' visual idea. It uses the game's own symbol, and it fits the original (00:62 'עומק ויזואלי'; animations as part of the experience).
- The only rule it breaks is a design-doc rule Claude wrote after round 1 (motion.md §1.4), so Moshe can change it with a new D-row.

Why it is not the biggest lever:
- The flat feeling comes mainly from transparent controls (1.44:1 hairlines, Button.tsx:288-294) and cards at 1.09:1. A moving background behind cards that already melt into the ground makes the screen muddier, not richer.
- The recommended ink is 1.01:1 against surface, so a digit passing a borderless card looks like a bump on the card's edge. Fix the surfaces first.

Recommended version:
- Variant A 'light': 9 neutral grey digits in a solid precomposited ink, never seat colours or gold (that keeps them distinct from the Scramble interference and from the gold actions).
- At least half resting at any moment. Behaviours: walk, pause, the occasional hop, look around.
- Skip B's line-up moment in v1. It could later become a post-win reaction.
- Screens: Home, Login/Register, and Match search at half count only. Never on a board screen, the 3-2-1 countdown, or History and Leaderboard.

Must-haves, each with a test:
- Pause on blur: Home stays mounted under the game.
- Settle after about 25 s without a touch: keepScreenOn is true everywhere.
- Load Skia lazily after the first screen.
- A static frame under Reduced Motion. Moshe still gets his texture, with no motion.

Ship the static base (top light and brand grid) regardless. It gives most of the depth for almost no cost.

Plan: a 1-day prototype on Home with a /dev/ambient tuning screen, judged by Moshe in a release build on his phone, because faintness on OLED versus LCD can't be judged from code. Then 3-4 days. If he finds A busy, fall back to C, which moves only while scrolling. It is the first thing to cut if time runs short.
critic.viewOnDigitAvatars:
The concept is the best brand idea on the table. In a sudoku game the fighters are the digits, and no mainstream sudoku app does this. It is also an evolution, not a restart: a full 0-9 digit family already exists in the catalog.

But I agree with the evaluation's hard diagnosis: the current set looks bland mostly because of presentation and house style, not the subject.
- Avatars appear at 28-36 px in a game.
- Gimmicks never play below 48 px.
- The most common reaction moves less than 1 px.
- The winner is 28 px, and Home never idles.
Digit characters drawn under the same flat rules and shown at the same sizes will look just as bland. So the presentation fixes (Phase 0) go before the store: they help any set.

Don't block the store release on the series. Three or four series at the 'very invested' level are about 5-8 weeks. Instead:
- Build a vertical slice now: Pirates 1 and 7 in two looks, shown on a board mock with 3 opponent locks.
- Let Moshe judge it on his phone.
- If it lands, ship 3 series plus the existing digits as 'Originals' in 1.2. Migrating after launch remains feasible through the normalizeAvatarId chain and the new version gate; it is cheaper before launch, and that trade-off is his.

Non-negotiables:
- The 22 dp avatar in an opponent-locked cell must never be a whole numeral (it reads as a placed digit, and scramble paints fake digits). Use a face crop or a seat-glyph disc.
- Each series gets its own letterform, or it becomes 'the same 7 in nine hats'.
- Fix the cast: a role for every digit, balanced genders, a long or pointy nose rather than a hooked caricature, no guns.
- Keep the 5 practice bots as non-digit characters.

Candidly, Duolingo-level character animation needs a human illustrator for the masters, and a Rive animator for full rigs. Claude-authored SVG produced the current set in about 3 days and has a real ceiling. The original's §33 ('אני אספק תמונות של אווטרים') already assumed Moshe would supply the art, so illustrator masters with Claude rigging and integrating fit his original intent best.
